regional_compliance.tax_context: Sales tax varies by state and locality, no federal VAT/GST. Restaurants generally pay state/local sales tax on prepared food, collected from the customer.
regional_compliance.labor_regulation: Federal minimum wage plus state-specific minimums (often higher); tip credit rules vary significantly by state — some allow a lower base wage for tipped employees, others (e.g. California) do not.
regional_compliance.licensing_bodies: Local health department (food safety permit), state liquor authority (if serving alcohol), local business license, EIN from IRS for tax purposes.
key_compliance_terms: state Department of Revenue sales tax filing

humanity_mode_regional_addendum.0_percent: State and local sales tax application to prepared food, federal vs. state minimum wage and tip credit interaction, local health department permit renewal cycles.

learning_objectives: Understand how sales tax on prepared food varies by state and locality, and how it differs from a VAT/GST system.
Analyze how tip credit rules affect labor cost calculations differently across US states.
